script.base: Carolina is the -5.5 favorite with a 22.0 implied total in a low 38.5 outdoor game, so the base script is a one-score Panthers lead by the half that closes on the ground. Rico Dowdle has taken the lead-back share over weeks 7-9 (50 carries, 263 yards, 5.26 YPC) ahead of Chuba Hubbard (31 carries, 82 yards, 2.65 YPC), and that is who gets the late clock-killing carries. New Orleans, implied 16.5, trails and has to throw, but the run game is already thin — Alvin Kamara only 23 carries for 63 yards in those three weeks, Taysom Hill 8/32 — and both Saints tackles (Taliese Fuaga, Barry Wesley) are out, so catch-up drives are pressured and inefficient rather than a shootout.
script.flip1: New Orleans scores first or stays within a score on explosives. Rashid Shaheed has 30 targets and 356 air yards over weeks 7-9 and Chris Olave has 218 yards on 23 targets, so a couple of 20-plus shots (Carolina has allowed 25 such passes for 294 yards in 9 games) flips the lead. Carolina then cannot hand Dowdle a 16-carry close, and Bryce Young's dropbacks get worse because the Saints blitz 35% and Carolina's EPA per dropback is -0.20 when blitzed versus -0.04 when not.
script.flip2: Defensive slog or weather drag. The forecast was not saved, and the roof is outdoors, so wind or rain is an unchecked under lean. Both offenses three-and-out: Dowdle never sees the carry spike, and the Saints' messy QB room — Spencer Rattler 5 rushes/24 yards and Tyler Shough 4/14 in the same three-week window — never stacks catch-up receiving yards either. Starters are only mildly blowout-risked at -5.5, not at a 10-point flag.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC, man/zone, or coverage chart in the pack, so receivers cannot be mapped to named zone defenders. Carolina blitzes only 25%, which is not a pressure shell; the Saints blitz 35%. Shell read is limited to location YPA and blitz splits below.
matchup.pressure: New Orleans EPA/db is -0.07 versus the blitz and -0.16 versus no blitz, so the Saints are poor either way and not specifically blitz-fragile; the real pressure is self-inflicted with Fuaga and Wesley out. Carolina EPA/db is -0.20 when blitzed versus -0.04 when not, and the Saints blitz 35%, so Panthers dropbacks are the fragile side. That supports a run-lean Carolina script and caps deep Saints yards more than it caps a lead-back rushing total.
matchup.bleeds: Carolina defense, 9 games: 4.74 rush YPC, only 22 runs of 10+, 25 passes of 20+ for 294 yards; YPA left 6.78 on 119 attempts, middle 8.95 on 59, right 6.02 on 102. Saints defense, 9 games: 4.31 rush YPC, 32 runs of 10+, 24 passes of 20+ for 276 yards; YPA left 7.0 on 115, middle 8.16 on 44, right 8.04 on 98. Carolina bleeds the middle of the field; New Orleans bleeds explosive runs and the middle/right pass.
matchup.overlap: The overlap that is actually in the pack is Dowdle's 62% share of Dowdle-plus-Hubbard carries (50 of 81) into a Saints front allowing 4.31 YPC and 32 explosive runs, with Bresee questionable. The pass overlap is weaker: Carolina's soft spot is middle YPA 8.95, which fits Johnson's 9.2 air yards per target (175 air on 19 targets) more than a named outside corner, and no chart says Olave (13.8 aDOT) or McMillan lines up there. Shaheed's 11.9 aDOT on 30 targets is the profile the missing tackles hurt.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both leans lost. Dowdle finished under 54.5 because Zavala was out, Hubbard still took about 10 carries, and the Saints' 35% blitz turned Carolina's -0.20 blitz EPA into short drives; the 54-yard game in the last four was the real baseline and the 183 and 130 were single explosives the median had already faded. Kamara went over 56.5 because he was healthier than the ankle tag, the game stayed close, Carolina's 4.74 YPC let a 12-carry day plus one checkdown spike repeat the 76-yard rush-plus-rec game, and Hill did not vulture the red-zone or late carries. Either result is live. That is why both are leans, flagged for no price, and not sized. Inactives 90 minutes before kickoff would have voided Kamara if he sat, and a saved wind forecast at 15-plus mph would have been the slog flip that also threatens Dowdle's carry count.
slip_story: One story only: Carolina leads and runs, New Orleans trails and does not feed Kamara. Legs that win together are Dowdle rush yards over and Kamara rush-plus-rec under. No touchdown legs, no receptions, one market per player, two legs, not padded to four. No bet placed. Re-check inactives before this would ever be a ticket.
